## Persistent block-filesystem telemetry with explicit availability

- Linux agents now total only mounted, positively verified persistent block
  filesystems. Pseudo, memory, overlay, network, FUSE, loop, RAM, and zram
  mounts are excluded; aliases and subvolumes of the same device are counted
  once, while distinct persistent partitions remain additive.
- Disk collection carries an explicit versioned availability contract. A
  failed, incomplete, or unversioned collection is unavailable instead of
  being reported as healthy zero usage. An explicit zero-capacity inventory
  remains an available fact but contributes no utilization value or weight.
  Custom collectors must opt in to the same contract explicitly.
- Minute, retained, alert, API, and console consumers use an independent disk
  sample count, so unavailable or legacy numeric values cannot dilute disk
  utilization or capacity history.

## Durable mutation and terminal lifecycle reliability

- Id-less policy, generator, webhook, and notification retries preserve the
  original identity and do not reset versions, arming state, timestamps, or
  audit evidence. Mutation responses are hydrated from the committing
  transaction rather than from a later writer's state.
- Authentication rotation, agent heartbeat, terminal sessions, job outputs,
  target/job completion, routing evidence, and backup artifact handling now
  keep their authoritative state and durable retry evidence atomic. Exact
  replays repair deferred work without duplicating lifecycle effects.
- Lock ordering and cancellation behavior are consistent across concurrent
  dispatch, expiry, reconnect, revoke, and terminal paths. Bounded spawned
  work is aborted with its parent, and large debug futures run from safe task
  roots without detached mutations.

## Release and operator safeguards

- The release workflow verifies a successful main-branch CI run for the exact
  annotated tag commit before building or publishing artifacts.
- Monitoring, alert, configuration, schedule, and audit console contracts have
  stricter keyboard, accessibility, stale-evidence, and resource-scoped test
  coverage across desktop and mobile layouts.
- Database migrations now run through `0014`. A v0.4.5 database applies only
  compatibility migration `0014`; exact v0.4.4 and v0.3.5 baselines apply
  `0010`-`0014` and `0009`-`0014`, respectively. Existing legacy disk numbers
  remain stored but have disk sample count zero and stay inert until a new
  versioned agent sample arrives; raw unavailable disk totals become nullable.
  Back up and test the database, drain webhook work, stop all old writers for
  the complete migration, and start only v0.4.6 writers after commit.
